recommendations: Send the men’s email to all customers. At the base contact cost, it gives the most profit of all rules (Step 7a).

Confirm the full contact cost before the launch. If Marketing confirms a cost of $0.25 or more, send only to the top 25% by history (Step 7a). If the cost is more than $0.23, “send to all” loses money.
Keep a 10% holdout. It shows with 87% power that the email still pays for itself, and it costs $1,309 for each campaign (Step 7d).

answer: Send the men’s email to all customers. It increases the mean spend by $0.77 for each customer (95% CI [$0.49, $1.05]). For each campaign of 100,000 customers, it gives $13,095 of incremental profit, with a range of $4,554 to $21,635. It gives $10,362 more than the women’s email.

The policy passes 5 of the 5 branches of the evaluation framework. The branches that fail are: none. At the base contact cost of $0.10, no targeting rule and no ML uplift model beats “send to all”. A shorter list pays only if the full contact cost is $0.25 or more.
